shots.say: What is inside a camel's hump?
And why does baby Sandy have no hump at all?
I'm Milo. Let's find out together!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we fly to the hot, sandy desert.
Here we are! Look who is waiting for us.
This is Sandy, the baby camel. And this is her mama.
Look at the big hump on Mama's back.
It is tall and round, like a little hill of sand.
How many humps does Mama have? One!
Some camels have one hump. Some camels have two.
Can you make a hump with your arms? Up, and over!
Sandy looks up at the hump. What is in there?
Is it full of water, like a big water bottle?
Or is it full of fat?
What do you think? Is it water, or is it fat?
It is fat! A camel's hump is full of fat.
Not water. Fat!
Say it with me. Fat, not water!
The fat is food, saved for later.
It is like a backpack full of snacks.
When a camel cannot find food, the fat feeds her.
The fat gives the camel energy.
Energy to walk, and walk, and walk!
And water? A camel drinks it. Slurp!
A thirsty camel can drink up to thirty-two gallons at one time!
Glug, glug, glug! Can you drink like a camel?
Then a camel can go a week or more without water.
Sandy has a drink, too. Let's count her sips. One, two, three!
So the water is for drinking. And the hump is full of fat!
Mama and Sandy walk down the rocky trail.
Sandy is hungry. Mama is hungry, too.
Look! A thorny bush. Those thorns are sharp.
But camels have tough lips. Mama can eat thorny plants!
Munch, munch, munch! Can you munch like Mama?
A camel's hump can change its size.
When a camel eats a lot, the hump is big and tall.
It is full of fat. A full backpack!
But sometimes, there is not much food in the desert.
Then the camel's body uses the fat in the hump.
The hump gets smaller, and smaller.
And it leans over. Flop!
Can you flop over like a hump? Flop!
A tall hump is full of fat. A floppy hump has used it up.
This camel found no food for a long time. Is her hump tall, or floppy?
Floppy! She used the fat in her hump.
What will make her hump stand up again?
Food! The camel eats, and eats, and eats.
And the hump sits up tall again. Pop!
Mama had a big lunch today. Is her hump tall? Yes, it is!
With a full hump, a camel can last for several months without food!
Months and months! Thank you, hump!
Now look at baby Sandy. Where is her hump?
No hump! Just a little bump.
And on top, a tuft of curly hair.
Curly, curly, curly! Like a little hat.
Can you draw a curl in the air? Round and round!
Mama has a big hump. Sandy has a little tuft.
A baby camel is born with no hump.
In just half an hour, Sandy could walk beside her mama!
Step, step, step! Off they go.
Sandy stays close to her mama.
A baby camel drinks her mama's milk.
Sip, sip, sip! Can you sip like Sandy?
Mama and Sandy hum to each other. Listen!
Can you hum like a camel? Your turn!
Well done! You hum like a camel.
Was Sandy born with a hump? Yes, or no?
No! Just a little tuft of curly hair.
The tuft shows where her hump will grow.
As Sandy grows up, her hump will grow, too.
Bigger, and bigger, and bigger!
One day, Sandy will have a hump just like Mama's.
And it will be full of fat!
The sun goes down. Time to remember what we learned!
What is inside a camel's hump? Water, or fat?
Fat! It is food, saved for later.
When a camel finds no food, does her hump stand tall, or flop over?
It flops over. Flop!
Was baby Sandy born with a hump? Yes, or no?
No! Just a little curly tuft.
Good night, Sandy. Good night, Mama.
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
